methodological_rigor.justification: The study employs a rigorous multi-platform approach: TCGA-BRCA and GSE21653 bioinformatics with ssGSEA; protein-level validation via TMA (120 patients, IHC H-scoring); flow cytometry; co-IP + mass spectrometry identifying 83 TSPAN13/HLA-A2 interacting proteins; OT-1 adoptive transfer in vivo model; CD8+ T cell depletion and MHC-I blocking rescue experiments; cycloheximide chase for protein stability; endosome isolation with Western blot; bafilomycin A1 lysosome inhibition; and combination immunotherapy survival experiments. Statistical methods include two-tailed t-tests, one-way and two-way ANOVA with Tukey correction, Wilcoxon rank-sum, log-rank Mantel-Cox, and Kaplan-Meier analysis. Most in vitro experiments are n=3 biological replicates; in vivo experiments use n=4-7 per group. Limitations include the lack of a validated small-molecule TSPAN13 inhibitor for translational studies, some mechanistic Western blots showing only representative images without n≥3 quantification, and the adoptive transfer experiment limited to n=4 per group.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: This is a preclinical mechanistic study (LOE 5) with strong clinical translational hooks. The TMA analysis of 120 breast cancer patient specimens provides protein-level in-human evidence of TSPAN13-CD8+ T cell inverse correlation. The combination of TSPAN13 knockdown with anti-PD-L1 in the 4T1 syngeneic model demonstrates survival benefit relevant to the clinical challenge of ICI resistance in breast cancer. The analysis of TCIA immunophenoscores indicating higher predicted ICI response in TSPAN13-low patients provides a clinically actionable biomarker hypothesis. The identification of TSPAN13 as a new mechanism of MHC-I degradation via STUB1 recruitment addresses the understudied question of why breast cancers downregulate MHC-I independent of transcriptional silencing.

reporting_quality.justification: Animal experiments are conducted under IACUC approval (First Hospital of Jilin University, JDYY20240440) and follow ARRIVE guidelines with sex-stratified female mouse use, specified group sizes, and described endpoints. Human TMA use is IRB-approved (2023-395, First Hospital of Jilin University) with written informed consent and Declaration of Helsinki compliance. Cell lines are authenticated by STR profiling and Mycoplasma-tested within 3 months of resuscitation. All antibodies and reagents include catalog numbers and RRID identifiers. Statistical methods are fully specified. Gaps include: raw data for Western blot quantifications not consistently n=3 in all mechanistic experiments; TCGA/GEO datasets referenced but no original data deposition accession for the study itself; formal power calculations absent for in vivo experiments.

novelty_literature.justification: TSPAN13's role in MHC-I regulation is novel: while STUB1-mediated MHC-I ubiquitination was recently reported (Chen et al. 2023, Cell), this study is the first to identify TSPAN13 as a membrane-associated scaffold that enhances STUB1-MHC-I interaction, promoting MHC-I ubiquitination and lysosomal trafficking. The TSPAN13-STUB1-MHC-I tripartite complex represents a previously undescribed mechanism of post-translational MHC-I downregulation distinct from transcriptional silencing pathways. The functional consequence — TSPAN13 knockdown synergizing with anti-PD-L1 — is clinically relevant. The study also provides the first protein-level epidemiological evidence of the TSPAN13-CD8+ T cell inverse relationship across 120 patient specimens, and extends the mechanism to pancreatic cancer via external dataset reanalysis. The novelty is meaningful though partly incremental to the STUB1-MHC-I axis.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is logically organized from discovery bioinformatics through mechanistic dissection to in vivo therapeutic validation. The narrative clearly progresses from TSPAN13 identification, to its inverse correlation with MHC-I and CD8+ T cells, to the molecular mechanism (STUB1 recruitment, ubiquitination, lysosomal trafficking), and finally to immunotherapy combination efficacy. Discussion appropriately contextualizes findings within the STUB1-MHC-I axis and acknowledges limitations including lack of pharmacological TSPAN13 inhibitor. Methods detail is excellent with RRID identifiers throughout. Minor weaknesses: the manuscript mentions a correlation with XBP1 and HLA-E that is relegated to supplementary data without meaningful mechanistic follow-up, and some in vivo figure legends reference extensive supplementary figures for key data.

key_strengths: Novel mechanism identifying TSPAN13 as a membrane scaffold that recruits STUB1 to MHC-I, promoting ubiquitination and lysosomal degradation, validated by co-IP, mass spectrometry, endosome isolation, bafilomycin chase, and confocal colocalization

Comprehensive multi-platform validation: TCGA bioinformatics, 120-patient TMA protein-level analysis, multiple murine breast cancer models (4T1, E0771), OT-1 adoptive transfer, and CD8+ T cell depletion/MHC-I blocking rescue experiments
Clinically actionable finding: TSPAN13 knockdown combined with anti-PD-L1 significantly improves survival in 4T1 syngeneic model, directly relevant to ICI resistance in breast cancer
TCIA immunophenoscore analysis demonstrating TSPAN13-low patients have higher predicted ICI response provides testable clinical biomarker hypothesis
key_concerns: No pharmacological TSPAN13 inhibitor data; all functional evidence is based on genetic knockdown, limiting translatability and leaving the therapeutic hypothesis incomplete

The mechanism by which TSPAN13 specifically recruits STUB1 (versus other E3 ligases) to MHC-I is not fully resolved; TSPAN13 knockdown increases MHC-I more than STUB1 knockdown alone, implying additional uncharacterized ubiquitination pathways
In vivo experiments use n=4-7 per group which is adequate for efficacy but limits the power of immune phenotype subgroup analyses; the adoptive transfer experiment uses only n=4 per group
All in vivo models are syngeneic subcutaneous or orthotopic murine models; patient-derived xenograft models and humanized immune system models would strengthen translational confidence
chief_reviewer.rationale: This is a mechanistically thorough study revealing a novel TSPAN13-STUB1-MHC-I immune evasion axis in breast cancer with multi-platform validation spanning bioinformatics, 120-patient TMA, and in vivo immunotherapy combination experiments. Tier 2 reflects the mechanistic originality, strong in vitro and in vivo evidence, and clinical relevance to ICI sensitization in a cold tumor type, while the absence of a pharmacological inhibitor, limited in vivo group sizes, and partial mechanistic resolution constrain tier 1 consideration.
